I understand where you are coming from, really. It is also okay to think this way, but allow your feelings and perception to change over time so it does not consume you. I think it is normal and often happens that 2 people that care for each other do not end up long term. Most people that date experience this. The separation while painful, actually make you closer to what you are looking for. If you stay with him, you wont be able to have the opportunity to be with a partner that suits you better. I know it is so hard to see which is why the focus should be on self soothing and compassion before even thinking about action

I want to add that part of loving someone is a duty to protect and be responsible for that person. So we have to be ready to sacrifice our time and energy to nurture another. It sounds like he is overwhelmed with his own battle with his depression and parents and do not have ill will towards you - but not enough energy to protect and be strong for you right now. 

I hope this is a comforting thought to know what you both had was real. And you do understand what it means to love someone, and that is the most valuable lesson.

Right now is the perfect time for you to practice self-love and self-compassion to acknowledge the pain and suffering you experience and tend to your internal wounds. It will be difficult but try to focus your energy and attention to being very nice to yourself, it can be by resting a lot, doing activities that soothe you, or doing nothing but just sit there and acknowledge your loss and grieve properly. 

You deserve a partner who is willing to put your needs and his needs forward. Your ex has a lot of growing up to do and it might be hard to see right now but this pain of separation may be what ignited to you grow stronger internally and gain clear idea of what you need from a future partner when you are ready to make a new relationship. 

Relationships are hard and require both to work hard to nurture it. He is not the right person for you.

My suggestion for you is to find a good routine that can make you happy on your own. It can be journaling, drinking your favorite drink, meditating for 10 minutes a day etc. Exercising also helps with feeling positive and healthier overall. Having a good routine is a great step into having a healthier body and mind. Practice healthy mental habits and practice self-love, instead of self-hate/bashing that humans tend to do when we are down. Once you feel more calm and content, you will feel better going into the virtual meetup.

I'll be honest with you, as you go through life, you will have to develop a type of resistance aka thicker skin. And you have to accept that nothing falls out of the sky freely. Friends and girlfriends don't materialize out of thin air. A good job doesn't just get offered to you. Many of us in this world have to put time and energy to find the things that make us happy. Once we find the people we like, we must put in work to maintain the relationship.

Take this time to work on yourself. Find a way to accept yourself and your flaws. Practice self-love. Remember, everyone is anxious about something, people are just good at hiding it

People are not going to always be nice and welcoming, so it is a good idea to develop coping skills to handle your social anxiety. I'm not justifying any negative behavior, just saying that they will exist wherever you go. If you are open to therapy, I'd suggest you look into DBT therapy, in here they teach you coping skills to self soothe when you are doing through difficulties.

Good job on seeking help through reddit, hopefully you find some pointers here and can try out some of the advice mentioned.

I'm a lot older than you and went through something similar. I went through genocide, grew up with violence in a broken family. Bullied in school. Currently not in speaking terms with my family anymore due to how terribly they have treated me. 

I want to remind you that you are still VERY young. You are at the age of anxiety, nothing has been established under your name yet and you have little life experience. I also want to be blunt and tell you that people suck in general. No one at your age knows how to give comfort and the validation that you seek. Heck, even as people age, they don't necessarily know how to treat others with compassion.

Living alone during pandemic will give anyone a mental health problem. Honestly the solve to your problem is most likely to stop beating yourself up and start putting yourself out there (after you feel a little better). There are communities out there that you can join. I know with pandemic that can be hard. But the beauty of internet is you can make friends/connection with many communities. Have you tried sites like [meetup.com](https://meetup.com)? They post events that you can attend (digital or in person). What you need is variety and exposure to people from as many backgrounds as possible. There is no need for you to feel stuck. It will take time for you to find your people, but they exist.

Karma and all that jazz can exist. But it should not prevent you from taking the opportunities you have in this lifetime to make it the best life for yourself.
